result.instructions: Tools for Docparser, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which document parsers do I have set up in my account?"; "Show the parsed results of the last 5 documents in my invoice parser."; "Has my last uploaded document finished processing yet?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Docparser data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run docparser_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run docparser_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run docparser_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. docparser_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: docparser_ping
tools.title: Check API key
tools.description: Check that the connected Docparser API key works. Returns {msg: "pong"} when it does. GET /v1/ping.

tools.name: docparser_list_parsers
tools.title: List parsers
tools.description: List all Document Parsers on the account (id and label). Start here: the parser id is needed by every other tool. GET /v1/parsers.

tools.name: docparser_list_parser_models
tools.title: List parser model layouts
tools.description: List the model layouts of one parser (id and label). GET /v1/parser/models/{parser_id}.

tools.name: docparser_get_document_status
tools.title: Get document status
tools.description: Processing status of one document: importing/processing flags, page count, timestamps (uploaded, imported, processed), webhook dispatch and failed jobs. Poll this after a fetch/upload: the document is done when importing_in_progress and processing_in_progress are false, processed_at is set and failed_jobs is empty (a non-empty failed_jobs means it failed); then read the results. GET /v2/document/status/{parser_id}/{document_id}.

document_id.description: Docparser document id (the `id` / `document_id` of an uploaded document).

tools.name: docparser_get_document_results
tools.title: Get parsed data of one document
tools.description: The parsed data of one document (the fields and tables the parser extracted, plus file name, page count and upload/processing times). Docparser allows 60 of these calls per minute. GET /v1/results/{parser_id}/{document_id}.

document_id.description: Docparser document id (the `id` / `document_id` of an uploaded document).

include_children.description: Also return data of child documents created during preprocessing (for example split documents).

annotations.title: Get parsed data of one document

tools.name: docparser_list_document_results
tools.title: List parsed data of many documents
tools.description: Parsed data of several documents of one parser: the last uploaded ones (default), or those uploaded/processed after a date. Returns up to 100 documents per call; page with offset (next_offset is null on the last page). Docparser allows 30 of these calls per minute. GET /v1/results/{parser_id}.

list.description: Which documents (default last_uploaded). uploaded_after and processed_after need `date`.

date.description: ISO 8601 date-time (e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z) or a Unix timestamp. Required with list=uploaded_after or processed_after.

offset.description: Skip this many documents (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

remote_id.description: Only documents uploaded with this remote_id.

include_processing_queue.description: Also include documents that are not fully processed yet.

annotations.title: List parsed data of many documents

tools.name: docparser_fetch_document_from_url
tools.title: Import a document from a URL
tools.description: WRITE: ask Docparser to download a document from a publicly reachable URL and parse it with the given parser. Uses page credits of the account's plan (documents queue when credits run out). Docparser may buy extra credits by itself only if the account owner turned on automatic credit replenishment, or the account is on an annual plan that renews early when credits run out - check the Docparser billing settings first. This server never buys credits or changes the plan. Returns the new document_id: poll docparser_get_document_status, then read docparser_get_document_results. POST /v2/document/fetch/{parser_id}.

url.description: Public http(s) URL of the file (PDF, image, Word, Excel, CSV, ...).

remote_id.description: Your own reference for the document (stored by Docparser; usable as a filter later).

annotations.title: Import a document from a URL

tools.name: docparser_upload_document
tools.title: Upload a document (base64)
tools.description: WRITE: upload one small file as base64 content to a parser and parse it. Uses page credits of the account's plan. Docparser may buy extra credits by itself only if the account owner turned on automatic credit replenishment, or the account is on an annual plan that renews early when credits run out - check the Docparser billing settings first. This server never buys credits or changes the plan. Prefer docparser_fetch_document_from_url for large files. Returns the new document id and the remaining quota. POST /v1/document/upload/{parser_id}.

file_name.description: File name with extension (e.g. invoice.pdf); a time-based name is used if omitted.

remote_id.description: Your own reference for the document (stored by Docparser; usable as a filter later).

tools.name: docparser_reparse_documents
tools.title: Re-parse documents
tools.description: WRITE: run the parser again over already imported documents (for example after changing parsing rules). Replaces their parsed data. Re-parsing documents already in the account does not use additional credits. 1-50 document ids per call. POST /v1/document/reparse/{parser_id}.

items.description: Docparser document id (the `id` / `document_id` of an uploaded document).

document_ids.description: Ids of the documents to re-parse.

prompts.name: getting_started
prompts.title: Get started with Docparser
prompts.description: What you can do with Docparser here, with example requests to try.
